answer: A stake-backed identity bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if the agent cheats. A single honest agent stands on a knoll of reputation built over time, while an attacker flooding the market must fund a whole river of fake identities, each costing a real deposit. Like a falcon spotting one bird among many, auditors can trace bonds back to the same wallet and slash the lot at once.
